reason: The cited evidence does not address CrB coatings, reactive infiltration, or intermetallic barrier formation in molten aluminum. E1 describes HfC coatings on a HEA with cracks and pits but no Al infiltration; E2 discusses oxide layers in molten fluoride salts, not borides or Al corrosion; E3 covers chloride corrosion in molten salts, irrelevant to the premises. Thus, none of the key premises are supported by the cited passages.
premises: CrB-based boride coatings have inherent surface porosities and microdefects that act as corrosion pathways
Reactive infiltration of an Al-rich alloy at ~650°C can fill these defects
The infiltrated Al reacts with the boride to form a continuous, dense intermetallic barrier (e.g., Al3X-type phase)
This intermetallic barrier is thermodynamically stable and limits diffusion/chemical attack by molten Al
The barrier reduces molten Al corrosion by ~35% compared to untreated CrB coatings
